worked_solution:
We say $f(x)$ is of order $g(x)$ as $x\to a,$ and we write 

$$
f(x)=O(g(x))\,\text{as}\,x\to a
$$

if there exist $\text{positive}$ constants $K$ and $\delta $ such that

$$
|f(x)|\le K|g(x)|\,\text{for all}\,0<|x-a|<\delta .
$$

 

So, in our case, we need to show that

$$
|f(x)|\le K|x|\,\text{for}\,0<|x|<\delta .
$$

By the triangle inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|f(x)| & =|3{x}^{2}+x| \\  & \le |3{x}^{2}|+|x| \\  & =3|x{|}^{2}+|x|.\end{aligned}
$$

If $|x|<1,$ then we have $|x{|}^{2}<|x|.$ Therefore,

$$
3|x{|}^{2}\le 3|x|.
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}|f(x)| & \le 3|x{|}^{2}+|x| \\  & \le 3|x|+|x| \\  & =4|x|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $|f(x)|\le 4|x|$ whenever $|x|<1.$ Thus, taking $K=4$ and $\delta =1$ satisfies the definition, and we conclude that $f=O(x)$ as $x\to 0.$
